articles.title: Andy Burnham signals backing for more ethnicity options on next census
articles.summary: It comes after a Lib Dem MP said black English or Asian English should be specific options for respondents.
articles.body:
Andy Burnham has signalled his support for dedicated options at the next census to allow people to define themselves as black English or Asian English.

It comes after Liberal Democrat MP Josh Babarinde called for legislation to widen ethnicity options for respondents at the next population count, due in 2031.

The last census, held in 2021, saw English offered within a broader white category, but without specific options for black English or Asian English.

Asked at Prime Minister's Questions whether he would support Babarinde's proposal, Burnham said he had not seen details of the plan.

But he added: "I stand here thinking that I would want to support that bill, to directly take on the poisonous politics we've seen from some in this House".

"We must bring people back together. I am interested in working with anyone in this House who shares that aim," he added.

Burnham did not respond to a follow-up question from Lib Dem leader Sir Ed Davey about whether he would meet Babarinde to discuss his plan, and he did not specify whether the government would give it time for debate in Parliament.

Babarinde introduced his proposal for legislation on Tuesday, under a rule that allows MPs to propose new laws in a 10-minute speech.

Such draft laws, known as private members' bills, rarely become law without support from the government of the day but are often used by MPs to raise awareness of issues and generate media attention for policy ideas.

Census should include black English and Asian English options, says MP

Respondents to the 2021 census were asked a two-stage question about ethnicity, with options grouped under five broad ethnic headings.

In Wales, the terms "Asian Welsh" and "Black Welsh" were listed in the broad categories themselves, and respondents were able to pick "Welsh" as an option underneath the broader white category.

The form in England listed "English" as an option in the white ethnic category, but the only way for respondents to describe themselves as Black English or Black English was via a free-form text box.

In Scotland, the term "Scottish Asian" appeared in the broad categories, whilst "Black Scottish" was given as an example response for the text box.

Speaking on Tuesday, Babarinde said his proposed law would introduce Black English and Asian English as specific new categories, arguing that the text box on the current form "may as well be the margin".

Babarinde's proposal has been backed by some MPs in other parties, including Labour former deputy prime minister David Lammy and Conservative Sir James Cleverly, who quit the shadow cabinet this summer to run for London mayor.

The Eastbourne MP has previously told the BBC he put forward his bill in the wake of comments by former Conservative home secretary Suella Braverman, who defected to Reform UK earlier this year.

Braverman wrote in 2015 that she was British Asian but said she "cannot claim to be English" despite being born and educated in England.

She has reaffirmed her position in recent weeks, writing on X that Englishness was "an ethnicity" and it was "not racist to say this".

"To say I'm English is to take a 'laissez-faire, anything-goes' attitude to ethnicity, citizenship and identity. It also denies me my Asian heritage," she added.

The detailed questions asked during the census in England and Wales are set out in legislation following recommendations from the Office of National Statistics.

The law setting out the questions for the last census was passed around 10 months before it took place in March 2021. The Scottish government delayed the census in Scotland until the following year because of the Covid pandemic.

articles.title: Russia bans two French lawmakers, two journalists in tit-for-tat move
articles.summary: Kremlin spokeswoman says ban responds to the expulsion of a Russian commentator who used to head RT France.
articles.body:
Russia has blacklisted two French lawmakers and two French journalists in response to France’s expulsion of a pro-Kremlin media network commentator earlier this year.

Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova said on Wednesday that lawmakers Sacha Houlie and Arthur Delaporte would be banned from entering Russia, along with journalists Paul Gogo and Ariane Chemin.

Zakharova said the ban was for the alleged “harassment” of Xenia Fedorova, the head of RT France from 2017 to 2023.

French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot described Fedorova as an “agent of influence” and expelled her in July.

Fedorova, who wrote for right-wing French media, slammed “censorship” against her, while Moscow for months pledged to retaliate against “persecution”.

Ordering her expulsion in July, France’s Interior Minister Laurent Nunez had accused her of relaying Russian propaganda in an attempt to attack “the fundamental interests of the nation”.

Moscow has long bristled against European restrictions on its state-backed media and journalists, who Brussels and many countries in the European Union have slammed as Kremlin mouthpieces.

In a post on X, French lawmaker Sacha Houlie said: “What is intended as a sanction strikes me as recognition of my work against foreign interference in France.”

“From my report for the Parliamentary Intelligence Delegation to the law aimed at preventing interference that I had passed in 2024, right through to securing the expulsion of the Russian agent Fedorova,” Houlie added.

Russia has banned dozens of Western journalists and lawmakers from entering the country since it launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

articles.title: Dublin: Man charged after unrest following visit from former US President Biden
articles.summary: Joe Biden was in Dublin to see his son Hunter awarded the Gold Medal for Outstanding Contribution for Public Discourse
articles.body:
A man has been charged in relation to a "public order incident" following a visit by former US President Joe Biden to Trinity College in Dublin.

Biden was accompanied by former first lady Jill Biden as they attended a ceremony on Tuesday where their son Hunter was awarded the Gold Medal for Outstanding Contribution for Public Discourse.

During the trio's visit to the College Historical Society groups of pro-Palestinian protesters gathered, some of whom were detained by gardaí (Irish police).

Gardaí said the man, aged in his 50s, was one of three arrested on Tuesday. The other two men, one aged in his 30s and the other in his late teens, have been released without charge.

A number of garda officers and public order unit vans were on site at the university on Tuesday.

In 2024 Hunter Biden was convicted of gun and tax crimes in in the US but was later pardoned by his father while he was still president .

It made him the first child of a sitting president to be a convicted of a crime.

Previous recipients of the award include former Irish president Michael D Higgins, Bob Geldof, Patti Smith, Julian Assange and Desmond Tutu.

The former US president and his family also met with the Taoiseach (Irish prime minister) Micheál Martin.

Martin said on X that he had been pleased to welcome the family and that they reflected on Biden's "strong Irish roots".

articles.body: Lollapalooza has committed $1.7 million to Chicago Public Schools through 2031 to expand arts education, including music, dance and theatre programmes for young artists across the city. The grant was announced on 17 May 2026 and is one of the largest gifts the district has ever received for arts programming. It lifts the music festival’s total support for arts in the city’s public schools to $3.9 million since 2021. Two community partners, Ingenuity and Children First Fund, the Chicago Public Schools Foundation, are working closely with the district to deliver the festival’s donation across Chicago classrooms and into after-school ensembles.Lollapalooza grant to Chicago Public Schools splits across two arts education programmesAccording to Chicago Public Schools, the grant advances two initiatives. A new $634,000 investment goes to All-City Performing Arts, which runs after-school music, dance and theatre ensembles for students across Chicago. A $1.1 million renewal goes to the Lollapalooza Arts Education Fund, which gives schools grants to expand in-school arts programmes across artistic disciplines.The district says the two programmes together strengthen visual arts, music, dance and theatre during the school day while widening the chances for students to practise and perform outside it. It describes the funding as reflecting the festival’s long-term commitment to equitable arts education in every neighbourhood.Charlie Walker, a partner at C3 Presents and a Lollapalooza promoter, said in the announcement that investing in arts programmes for district students is one of the most impactful ways to help shape Chicago’s future. He said the aim is to make a real difference in classrooms and to give students new opportunities beyond school to learn, perform and share their talents.All-City Performing Arts, Chicago’s music, dance and theatre ensembles, gets a new $634,000 boostFounded in 1963, All-City Performing Arts serves students in grades 3 to 12, who rehearse every Saturday during the autumn and spring semesters with instruction from district arts educators. Children First Fund administers the new support. Of the $634,000, $134,000 pays for an instrument lending library that gives music students practice tools, and $500,000 covers rehearsal space, transport, supplies and performances.The programme has been reimagined as Lollapalooza Presents: All-City Performing Arts and was due to launch in autumn 2026, alongside the renewed fund.Macquline King, the district’s chief executive and superintendent, said in the announcement that access to instruments and rehearsal time outside school helps students practise consistently. She said the support lets the district maintain and widen its reach so that a student’s “zip code does not define their access” to high-quality artistic training and performance opportunities.Lollapalooza Arts Education Fund renewal keeps arts grants flowing to Chicago schools in needThe fund was established in 2021 through a $2.2 million donation to Ingenuity, its administrator, and its renewal runs through the 2028-29 school year. It supports in-school arts instruction, teaching artists and improvements to creative spaces in the schools with the greatest needs. By the time of the announcement, it had awarded 234 grants to 117 schools across 43 Chicago wards, reaching more than 80,000 students.Nicole Upton, executive director of Ingenuity, said in the Chicago Public Schools announcement that the festival’s support has been critical in expanding access to high-quality arts education in the schools that need it most. She said the renewal keeps resources reaching classrooms, strengthening programmes and supporting educators.Ingenuity and the district’s Department of Arts Education expect the investments across the fund and All-City Performing Arts to reach more than 40,000 students in more than 150 schools and more than 40 wards over five years. articles.title: What are the state of our grooming laws?
articles.summary: Some campaigners have been calling for the law to clearly define what grooming means.
articles.body:
Time and again since the international explosion of the "Me Too" movement in 2017 against sexual violence against women and girls, politicians have been pushed on whether we in the UK have an adequate list of crimes in place to deal with all manner of incidents.

Those demands for reviews and rethinks have come back again with the conviction of one comedian Russell Brand for rape and sexual assault - and separate accusations of sexual misconduct against another one, David Walliams. He denies being a sexual predator and is not facing a criminal investigation.

The modern landscape of sexual offences in England and Wales is complicated - but it is far more nuanced than it once was because of major changes over the last two decades.

There is some confusion in public debate over what counts as grooming - but in general it's understood in the criminal courts to refer to situations where a predator builds a relationship of trust with a child target in order to prepare the ground for sexual activity. Given the end goal, that relationship will often involve a great deal of manipulation - usually emotional, often subtle and regularly coercive.

Since 2003 it has been an offence for an adult to meet a child "following sexual grooming" and the maximum sentence is 10 years.

The crime is committed when an adult has met or communicated with someone under 16-years-old on at least one occasion and then intentionally meets them, or travels to meet them, with the intention of committing a sexual offence.

Jonathan Ross 'horrified' by Walliams allegations and Brand conviction

'I felt like I was being manipulated': Woman alleges Walliams groomed her as a teenager

David Walliams accused of sexual misconduct after losing injunction bid

There are other offences which generally cover some of the ground of grooming: arranging and facilitating a child sex offence, sexual communications with a child, causing a child to watch a sexual act or inciting an under 13-year-old to take part in one.

The offence gets little media attention, but analysis from the Centre of Expertise on Child Sexual Abuse, an independent body funded by the government to provide insights, shows that grooming offences are regularly turned to by the police and prosecutors.

Its latest report on crime statistics shows that 7,197 sexual grooming offences were recorded by the police across England and Wales in 2024/25.

Nearly a third of those ended up in a charge - and in 2024 just over 2,000 defendants were convicted. The rate of prosecuting suspects for grooming has more than doubled in seven years.

One final offence to highlight is the crime of abusing a position of trust for a sexual purpose with a child. This covers young people up to the age of 18 because the abuse may be taking place in a care environment.

Since June, grooming has been a specific element of sentencing law. Judges who are deciding a sentence for a child sex offender to consider how the contact came about - and if there was evidence of grooming, that becomes a factor to increase the length of the sentence.

So does that mean that the law is entirely settled and accepted? Well not quite.

Some campaigners have been calling for the law to clearly define what grooming means.

ThirtyOne:Eight, a charity consultancy that works on improving safeguarding in religious settings, said last year that its work had led it to conclude that the intention to groom - whether or not sexual abuse takes place - should become a self-standing crime.

And Baroness Louise Casey, who carried out a national audit of grooming gang abuse, highlighted another issue.

Sexual offences law includes a subtle exception for teenagers who have not yet reached the legal age of consent at 16 but who are in a relationship with each other. That nuance is designed to avoid needlessly criminalising 13 to 15-year-olds who seemingly know what they are doing.

But, says Casey in her report, there were "examples of perpetrators being charged with the lesser offence of 'sexual activity with a child', rather than rape, because of a belief that the child involved had 'consented' to having sex."

Speaking to the BBC Radio 4's Today Programme, she said that it was "staggering" that adults who have sex children aged 13, 14, and 15 are not automatically charged with rape, as is the case in France.

She has asked for that gap to be closed and told the BBC she had received an assurance from ministers this it would happen.

"The recommendations from the grooming gang audit that I did last year are works in progress," she said. "They're not completed yet, and obviously, I would like the government to press on with those."

The Ministry of Justice has been contacted for comment.

All of that is aimed at dealing with crimes against children and young teenagers. So is there space for changes elsewhere?

Some argue that the UK should have a "staggered" age of consent.

This became a talking point in 2023 after allegations against Russell Brand exploded over the media.

One of his alleged victims told BBC's Woman's Hour at the time that we should consider changing the law so that people over 18 would not be allowed to have sex with 16 and 17-year-olds.

"There's a reasonable argument [that] individuals between the ages of 16 and 18 can have relations with people within that same age bracket," she said. "You're allowed to make mistakes as a teenager, they should be with other people your own age."

The counter-argument to that is once someone is over the age of consent, the law already makes clear that they have the maturity to consent to sex. And if they have not given it, the law is clear: the act is not one of love, but rape.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) chief Asaduddin Owaisi and Azad Samaj Party (Kanshiram) president Chandrashekhar Azad are likely to announce an alliance for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections at a joint press conference in Lucknow on Thursday, November 12.The proposed tie-up could mark an attempt by the two parties to build a political front outside the BJP-led NDA and the Samajwadi Party-Congress alliance. Both parties are looking to consolidate support among Dalit and minority voters, who together account for nearly 41 per cent of Uttar Pradesh's electorate, according to the figures cited by party leaders.AIMIM spokesperson Shadab Chauhan confirmed that the two parties would join hands, but said details of the agreement would be made public at the press conference, news agency PTI reported.The event is expected to be held at a hotel in Gomtinagar and will be addressed by Owaisi and leaders of the Bhim Army.Both leaders have reached Lucknow ahead of the announcement. Asked about the proposed alliance, Azad said its aim was to strengthen the position of young people, farmers and marginalised sections. He said further details would be shared on Thursday.The parties have not yet disclosed how many of the state's 403 assembly seats they intend to contest. It is also unclear whether other smaller parties will join the proposed front.The development follows Owaisi's unsuccessful attempt to secure a place in the INDIA bloc's seat-sharing arrangement in Uttar Pradesh. The AIMIM chief had set an October 2 deadline for the Samajwadi Party and Congress to respond to his offer, but neither party agreed to include him in the alliance.While AIMIM has a limited electoral footprint in Uttar Pradesh, Owaisi has influence among sections of the minority community. Azad, the Nagina MP, has been seeking to expand his support among young Dalit voters. Their proposed partnership could therefore add another political equation to the contest, as the BJP looks to retain power for a third consecutive term and the opposition seeks to challenge it.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Portugal cancels more than 300 flights, shuts schools due to Storm Charles
articles.summary: Authorities spared no effort in preparation for the Atlantic storm after criticism following January’s Storm Kristin.
articles.body:
More than 300 flights in and out of Portugal have been cancelled, while businesses and all schools nationwide shut down before Storm Charles hit the country’s mainland, but the heavy rainfall and intense winds passed without causing severe damage.

Operations shut down on Wednesday across four different international airports, as well as hundreds of supermarkets and all non-essential public services across the country.

For the first time in living memory, about 8,000 of Portugal’s schools cancelled classes over the significant Atlantic storm forecast.

Streets were largely deserted when Storm Charles arrived, because the government had told people to stay at home, fearing the worst.

The national weather agency, IPMA, recorded wind gusts of more than 120km/h (75mph) in some areas.

Buses without passengers drove through the country’s capital, Lisbon, where some streets flooded due to clogged drains.

A national supermarket chain closed its stores, while the Web Summit technology conference in Lisbon, attended by about 70,000 people, called off the day’s events.

By mid-afternoon, only the southern Algarve region, a popular European tourist destination, remained on red alert, the highest level of emergency warning, which initially had covered more than half of the country.

Storm Charles had struck the Portuguese island of Madeira, off northwest Africa, on Tuesday with 130km/h (81mph) winds.

In January, the country’s centre-right government faced harsh criticism for its weak response when Storm Kristin hit central Portugal, felling thousands of trees and causing widespread property damage that is still being repaired.

In February, a 70-year-old man died in the southern region of Alentejo after flooding swept his vehicle off a street in the aftermath of Storm Leonardo.

Prime Minister Luis Montenegro chaired a crisis unit along with eight government ministers and other officials to monitor the storm.

Interior Minister Luis Neves, who oversees public safety, dismissed suggestions that authorities had overreacted, saying the government organised its response in accordance with the weather forecast.

Storm Charles was forecast to head later into Spain, where workers staged a general strike Wednesday. Strike organisers cancelled or postponed demonstrations in some southern cities, including Cordoba, Huelva and Cadiz.
